card: This PR updates SignPSBTInput to accept valid 65-byte Taproot signatures when no PSBT_IN_SIGHASH_TYPE constraint is present on the input. Currently, the missing field causes Bitcoin Core to impose a default 64-byte SIGHASH_DEFAULT constraint, rejecting valid self-describing 65-byte signatures and preventing valid Taproot PSBTs from finalizing. This bug affects users processing Taproot transactions constructed by external signers or descriptors with explicit sighash types, as tracked in issue #36507. Strict sighash matching is preserved whenever an explicit constraint is provided.
evidence: References issue #36507: 'PSBT: SignPSBTInput rejects valid 65-byte taproot script signatures when PSBT_IN_SIGHASH_TYPE is absent'
PR description: 'The existing check applies the locally assumed default to signatures that already specify their own sighash type. This can prevent valid Taproot PSBTs from being finalized.'
problem: Users and external signers submitting valid 65-byte Taproot signatures (which encode an explicit sighash byte) experience signing or finalization failures if the input omits the optional `PSBT_IN_SIGHASH_TYPE` field.

risk.why: A flaw in PSBT input signing and sighash handling could produce invalid signatures or improperly accept mismatched sighash types during PSBT processing.

scope_notes: The patch is small (+160/-2 across 3 files), with the bulk of the additions dedicated to regression tests for Taproot key-path, script-path, and mixed sighash spends.
summary: Updates `SignPSBTInput` to accept self-describing 65-byte Taproot signatures when `PSBT_IN_SIGHASH_TYPE` is omitted. Currently, an absent sighash field causes the signing logic to assume `SIGHASH_DEFAULT` (64 bytes), rejecting valid 65-byte signatures. Strict sighash checking is retained whenever an explicit sighash type is specified by the PSBT or caller.
